- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.2) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (sentiment < -0.4) — model underreacts to bearish signals.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays downward adjustments after a spike, especially if sentiment turns negative mid-horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to anticipate pullback unless sentiment shifts sharply.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile — adjust downward if sentiment is mixed or negative.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment shifts — model often misinterprets short-term sentiment as long-term trend.
